resources.string: A fact about any Twitch user, written {lookup.twitch:login.field}. Fields: game, title, isLive, viewers, display, avatar, createdAt, uptime, lastGame, url. The fields followers and followage:channel work for your own channel only. Example: Minecraft
The box art link of a Twitch category, written {lookup.game:name.boxart}. Example: https://static-cdn.jtvnw.net/ttv-boxart/27471-285x380.jpg
The most watched Twitch category right now: Just Chatting

The weather in a city, written {lookup.weather:city.field}. Fields: temp, temp.f, feels, condition, emoji, wind, humidity, tomorrow. Without a field it prints the city, the temperature and the condition. Off when the bot runs in saas mode. Example: Amsterdam: 12 °C, light rain
The local time in a city, written {lookup.time:city} with the optional fields date and offset. Off when the bot runs in saas mode. Example: 23:30
An amount in another currency, written {lookup.currency:amount|from|to}. Example: 10 EUR = 11.62 USD
The exchange rate between two currencies, written {lookup.currency.rate:from|to}. Example: 1.162
The day of the latest exchange rates, with an optional from|to pair (EUR|USD by default): 2026-10-26
A translation, written {lookup.translate:language|text} (from English) or {lookup.translate:from|to|text}. Example: goedemorgen
The text of the command (or the chat message) translated into a language, written {lookup.translate.chat:language}. The text is taken to be in the channel language. Example: good morning
